experimental: Persistent identifiers for materials, samples, and batches
Composition, structure, or physical description needed to understand the sample
Starting materials, sources, and lot identifiers when they affect the result
Preparation steps, time, temperature, pressure, medium, atmosphere, and sequence of operations
Instrument model and ID, method, calibration or verification evidence, and acquisition settings
Units, uncertainty where applicable, environmental conditions, and original raw files
Traceable chain from sample → measurement → file → processed result
computational: System or structure: species, coordinates, lattice or cell, and relevant boundary conditions
Method or model family and scientific approximations
Software or code, exact version, and input files
Influential numerical parameters: basis-set or pseudopotential choices, cutoffs, k-points, convergence criteria, and method-dependent smearing or spin settings
Workflow tasks, dependencies, inputs, and outputs
Environment and hardware details when they affect reproducibility
A parsed, normalized representation alongside raw inputs and outputs
interop: NOMAD Metainfo is an example of a structured schema that separates method, system, calculation, and workflow.
OPTIMADE is an example of an interoperability layer built on REST APIs and schemas for materials databases.
No single schema covers every material and measurement technique; domain profiles must be derived from the intended use case.
